name: Prune a shrub properly
blurb: Most pruning damage comes from cutting at the wrong time of year or hacking rather than shaping. The rules are simple once you know what a plant flowers on.
gear: Loppers and a pruning saw for thicker wood
steps: Learn the timing rule: shrubs that flower on old wood are pruned right after flowering; those flowering on new wood are pruned in late winter.
Start with the three Ds — dead, damaged and diseased — which is always safe to remove.
Remove crossing and inward-growing branches to open the centre to light and air.
Cut just above an outward-facing bud, at a slight angle away from it.
Never remove more than about a third in one season, and step back frequently to check the shape.
Clean your blades between plants to avoid spreading disease.
tips: Pruning a spring-flowering shrub in winter removes all this year’s flowers. Identify the plant first.
Leaving stubs invites die-back. Cut back to a bud or to the branch collar.
proof: A shrub you pruned that comes back healthier and flowers well the following season.
